name: Generation 1: the first ten

sprites.name: Bulbasaur
sprites.note: Already in the library; only its materials changed, to the standard ones: skin and spots Skin, bulb Petal. Mark Redo to keep the old settings.

sprites.name: Ivysaur
sprites.note: Skin and spots: Skin. Leaves: Leaf. Bud: Petal.

sprites.name: Venusaur
sprites.note: Skin and ear insides: Skin. Petals, their spots and the yellow center: Petal. Leaves: Leaf. Trunk: Bark.

sprites.name: Charmander
sprites.note: Skin and belly: Skin. Tail flame: Flame, brightest at the yellow core, its glow flickering with the drawn flicker. Its Alternate 1 is gone: in the game data it was only a still pose.

sprites.name: Charmeleon
sprites.note: Skin and belly: Skin. Tail flame: Flame, brighter than Charmander's. Its Alternate 1 is gone: its front was a still body, its back nearly a copy of Idle.

sprites.name: Caterpie
sprites.note: Body, underside, side rings, antenna and tail tip: Skin. The head's spots are its eyes (this sprite closes them): Eye. Nothing glows.

sprites.name: Charizard
sprites.note: The format demo's Charizard again, which looked better: hide with a soft sheen that lets no light through, a belly that lets a little light through, and wings with an extra brighter blue so they catch the light. Its Alternate 1 is gone (its back was a still pose while the front moved), and its flame's glow flickers.

sprites.name: Squirtle
sprites.note: Skin: Skin. Shell, belly plate and rim: Shell.

sprites.name: Wartortle
sprites.note: Ears and tail: Fur. Skin and cheek streaks: Skin. Shell, belly plate and rim: Shell.

sprites.name: Blastoise
sprites.note: Skin and lower jaw: Skin. Shell, belly plate, rim and cannons: Shell. The cannons are not metal (no source says so); choose in the materials question.

note: Second look. The skin no longer lets light through, which is what made it look slick. Every surface now uses one of a few standard materials, defined in the queue question "Materials for the first ten". Motion is the game's own.
